description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of five different BERT-based models—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE—across three downstream NLP tasks: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue), as evaluated in the paper “2-Tier SimCSE: Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings.” The vertical axis represents “Accuracy / Correlation,” ranging from 0 to 0.8 with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Each model is represented by a group of three adjacent bars, with the legend indicating the color coding for each metric. The 2-Tier SimCSE model achieves the highest STS Correlation (~0.81) and Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78), while also maintaining competitive Sentiment Accuracy (~0.49). Supervised_SimCSE follows closely in STS Correlation (~0.80) and Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78), with slightly lower Sentiment Accuracy (~0.48). Unsupervised_SimCSE shows moderate performance across all tasks, with STS Correlation around 0.71 and Paraphrase Accuracy near 0.77. The baseline models (Single-task_baseline and Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout) consistently underperform, particularly in STS Correlation (~0.50 and ~0.58 respectively), though they maintain relatively stable Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.79–0.78). The chart visually emphasizes the superiority of the 2-Tier SimCSE approach, especially for semantic similarity tasks, while highlighting the trade-off in sentiment classification performance across all models.
